answer:
This is not a Ceph capacity problem. The VM's root disk claim asks for a storage class that does not exist on ocpv-garnet.

In sandbox-j5wqc-sap-hana-lab, list_pvcs shows:
- hana-db01-rootdisk: Pending, 64Gi, storage class ocs-external-storagecluster-ceph-rbd-virtualization. Event: ProvisioningFailed: storageclass.storage.k8s.io "ocs-external-storagecluster-ceph-rbd-virtualization" not found.
- hana-db01-data: Bound, 250Gi, storage class ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd-virtualization.

list_storage_classes on ocpv-garnet returns three classes: ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd-virtualization (the default), ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd and ocs-storagecluster-cephfs. There is no ocs-external-storagecluster-ceph-rbd-virtualization. The "external" name is how the class is called on clusters that use an external Ceph. On ocpv-garnet the internal ODF class is named ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd-virtualization. The provisioner was never even asked for a volume, so space never came into it. The data disk in the same namespace bound a 250Gi volume on ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd-virtualization, which shows that Ceph on this cluster is provisioning fine.

Fix: recreate the root disk's DataVolume/PVC with storageClassName ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd-virtualization, or better, fix the lab template that hard-codes the external class name so the next order doesn't hit this. A PVC's storage class cannot be edited in place. I also can't make the change: query_ocpv_cluster only reads (list_pvcs, list_storage_classes, list_vms and similar), so someone with cluster access has to apply it.
